Enum Class CloudProviderType

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<CloudProviderType>
com.eqixiac.equinix.fabric.model.implementation.cloud.CloudProviderType
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<CloudProviderType>, Constable
public enum CloudProviderType extends Enum<CloudProviderType>
Enumeration of supported cloud providers for Equinix Fabric interconnection.

Each constant represents a cloud provider whose direct connectivity product can be integrated with Equinix Fabric connections. The enum provides the display name and the cloud provider's connectivity product name for reference.

Each constant also carries the set of terms a Fabric service profile may be named with for that provider — the Fabric product name, the corporate name, the constant name, and curated aliases — so that callers matching marketplace profiles to a provider can do so with matchesServiceProfileName(String) instead of guessing at one particular spelling. Real marketplace profiles are named after the product ("AWS Direct Connect", "Azure ExpressRoute"), not after the corporation ("Amazon Web Services"), so matching on a single name is not sufficient.

What counts as evidence

A profile-name match is used to decide that a cloud is reachable from a metro, so a false positive is worse than a false negative: it silently promises an on-ramp that does not exist. The alias sets are therefore restricted to terms that are distinctive to the provider:

  • Admissible — coined brand tokens unique to the provider (aws, azure, expressroute, gcp, oci, fastconnect, aliyun), including their spaced spellings (express route, fast connect), and corporate names whose Fabric presence is that corporation's cloud (amazon, google, oracle, ibm, alibaba).
  • Not admissible — descriptive product phrases assembled from ordinary industry words: "direct connect", "direct link", "express connect", "cloud interconnect", "partner interconnect", "dedicated interconnect". Network service providers brand their own on-ramps with exactly these words, so "<NSP> Direct Connect" is not evidence of AWS.
  • Not admissible — microsoft on its own: Microsoft's Fabric presence is broader than Azure ("Microsoft 365"), so the bare corporate token does not identify an ExpressRoute on-ramp.

Every real product name still resolves, because each one carries a brand token: "AWS Direct Connect" and "Amazon Web Services Direct Connect" both match AWS, "IBM Cloud Direct Link" matches IBM_CLOUD, and seller-prefixed or region-suffixed variants ("Equinix AWS Direct Connect", "AWS Direct Connect - Sydney") match too.

  • Enum Constant Details

    • AWS

      public static final CloudProviderType AWS
      Amazon Web Services — Direct Connect. Uses AWS Account ID as the authentication key.

      "direct connect" is deliberately not an alias: it is a phrase many network service providers brand their own on-ramps with.

    • AZURE

      public static final CloudProviderType AZURE
      Microsoft Azure — ExpressRoute. Uses ExpressRoute Service Key (GUID) as the authentication key.

      The bare token "microsoft" is deliberately not an alias: Microsoft sells Fabric profiles that are not ExpressRoute on-ramps ("Microsoft 365").

    • GOOGLE_CLOUD

      public static final CloudProviderType GOOGLE_CLOUD
      Google Cloud Platform — Cloud Interconnect. Uses GCP Pairing Key as the authentication key.

      "cloud interconnect", "partner interconnect" and "dedicated interconnect" are deliberately not aliases: they are generic interconnection wording. Every Fabric profile for this product carries "Google" or "GCP".

    • ORACLE_CLOUD

      public static final CloudProviderType ORACLE_CLOUD
      Oracle Cloud Infrastructure — FastConnect. Uses Oracle OCID of the virtual circuit as the authentication key.

    • IBM_CLOUD

      public static final CloudProviderType IBM_CLOUD
      IBM Cloud — Direct Link. Uses IBM Cloud Direct Link identifier as the authentication key.

      "direct link" is deliberately not an alias: like "direct connect" it is generic carrier wording rather than evidence of IBM.

    • ALIBABA_CLOUD

      public static final CloudProviderType ALIBABA_CLOUD
      Alibaba Cloud — Express Connect. Uses Alibaba Cloud Account ID as the authentication key.

      "express connect" is deliberately not an alias: it is two ordinary industry words rather than a coined brand token. Fabric names this profile "Alibaba Cloud Express Connect", which matches on "alibaba".

    • OTHER

      public static final CloudProviderType OTHER
      Custom or unlisted cloud provider. Use this for providers not covered by the built-in constants.

      Deliberately carries no match terms: it is a placeholder, not a nameable provider, so matchesServiceProfileName(String) always returns false for it. Identify such providers by service profile name or UUID instead.

    • matchesServiceProfileName

      public boolean matchesServiceProfileName(String serviceProfileName)
      Returns true when the given Fabric service profile name identifies this provider.

      Matching is case-insensitive and token-aware: the profile name and every match term are normalized to lower-case, single-space-separated alphanumeric tokens, and a term matches only where it appears in the profile name on whole-token boundaries. That keeps short terms such as "aws" from matching inside unrelated words — the Warsaw metro and a profile named "Kawasaki" do not satisfy a required-AWS constraint — while seller prefixes and region suffixes are tolerated ("Equinix AWS Direct Connect", "AWS Direct Connect - Sydney").

      Matching is one-directional only: the profile name must contain a match term, never the other way round. A profile whose name is merely a sub-phrase of one of this provider's terms — "Web Services", "Cloud Platform", "Cloud Infrastructure", "Direct Connect" — does not resolve, because such a name is equally consistent with a third-party seller's own product and claiming a cloud is reachable where it is not is the more damaging error.

      Parameters:
      serviceProfileName - the Fabric service profile name; null is tolerated
      Returns:
      true if the name identifies this provider

    • shortCode

      public String shortCode()
      A compact, wire-safe token for this provider — aws, azure, gcp, oci, ibm or alibaba — suitable for composing Fabric resource names that must stay within Fabric's 24-character limit.

      Distinct from Enum.name() lower-cased, which would yield google_cloud and oracle_cloud rather than the conventional gcp/oci. OTHER, a placeholder rather than a nameable provider, returns the generic cloud.

      Returns:
      the short provider token, always non-blank and already lower-case
